GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2444 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
Groundwater Recharge through Community Forests 
2444. SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH: 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any initiative to scientifically link afforestation 
with groundwater recharge and watershed restoration in water-stressed regions of the 
country, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any policy has been formulated for developing community recharge forests on 
degraded Government land through participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions and local 
communities, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the steps taken to monitor the environmental and hydrological impact of such plantations 
using geospatial technology and remote sensing; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to identify suitable areas in the Bhiwani–
Mahendragarh Lok Sabha Constituency for establishment of Community Recharge 
Forests under the said initiative, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) The Government promotes afforestation as an integral component of watershed 
management, river rejuvenation and groundwater recharge through various 
programmes. Afforestation, soil and moisture conservation, catchment treatment and 
restoration of degraded landscapes are undertaken in convergence with water 
conservation initiatives to enhance infiltration, reduce soil erosion and improve 
hydrological functions in water-stressed areas. The Green India Mission (GIM), one 
of the Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), 
promotes restoration of degraded forests and ecosystems through afforestation, 
assisted natural regeneration and soil and moisture conservation measures, which 
contribute to improved watershed functions and groundwater recharge. These efforts 
are complemented by the Aravalli Green Wall Initiative through convergence with 
GIM, CAMPA, MGNREGS and State schemes 
(b) Under GIM, restoration activities are implemented through participatory planning 
involving Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), Gram Panchayats and 
other local institutions, wherever applicable. No separate policy has been formulated 
for development of "community recharge forests". However, the Mission supports 
restoration of degraded forests and other eligible lands through community 
participation. 
(c) GIM envisages the use of remote sensing, geo-tagging and periodic monitoring for 
planning and assessment of restoration activities, supplemented by independent 
evaluations undertaken from time to time. 

(d) As per information received from the Government of Haryana, bio-drainage 
plantations are being raised in waterlogged areas of Bhiwani district. Under the Green 
India Mission, implementation areas are identified by the respective State 
Governments/UT Administrations based on ecological priorities, approved 
Perspective Plans and availability of funds. Bhiwani and Mahendragarh districts fall 
within the Aravalli Green Wall landscape, where activities are taken up by the State 
Government through convergence with ongoing schemes, as per approved plans.

entries.t: Vacancies in Teaching and Non-Teaching Posts in University of Delhi
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2447 
ANSWERED ON- 03.08.2026 
 
Vacancies in Teaching and Non-Teaching Posts in University of Delhi 
 
†2447. Shri Ramvir Singh Bidhuri: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that there are a large number of vacancies in teaching and non-teaching 
posts in the University of Delhi and its affiliated colleges; 
(b) if so, the stream -wise details of vacancies across all departments and colleges of the 
University; and 
(c) the number of posts out of these vacant posts which are reserved for Other Backward 
Classes (OBCs), Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs)? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to ( c): University of Delhi is a statutory autonomous organizations established under 
Delhi University Act 1922 and governed by provisions of the Acts and Statutes, 
Ordinances, Regulations made thereunder. Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a 
continuous process. The vacancies a rise due to promotion, retirement, resignation and 
additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength etc.  The Central 
Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers Cadre) Act, 2019 has been notified on 
09.07.2019 which provides for rese rvation of posts in direct recruitment for persons 
belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes 
(OBCs), and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in the Teacher’s Cadre of Central 
Educational Institutions established, maintained, or aided by the Central Government. This 
Act removes the difficulty regarding the reservation of posts in appointment by treating 
University/Central Educational Institution as a unit for the purpose of reservation instead 
of individual department s. Further, by this Act from the year 2019, reservation was 
provided to Other Backward Class (OBC) in recruitment in Associate Professor and 
Professor level. Earlier reservation to OBC was only in Assistant Professor level. Posts 

reserved for a particular category can only be filled by eligible persons of that particular 
category; any unfilled post belonging to any of the reserved category will continue to be 
readvertised as backlog vacancies in that particular reserved category in next cycle(s) of 
recruitment, until filled. Further, the UGC launched a unified recruitment portal i.e. CU -
Chayan on 02.05.2023 to provide a common platform for listing of vacancies/ 
advertisements/ jobs across all Central Universities. The Central Universities have also 
been instructed to publish rolling advertisements on their websites throughout the year to

entries.t: Projects under NCF in Andhra Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2450 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
PROJECTS UNDER NCF IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
2450. SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY:  
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has identified two projects, first one is removal and resetting 
of approach steps to the Hill Fort at Udayagiri and the second one is removal and 
resetting of ancient flooring inside the Ranganayakula temple in Udayagiri, in Nellore 
district of Andhra Pradesh under the National Culture Fund (NCF); 
 
(b) whether it is true that the said projects are going to be taken up under CSR initiative 
through NCF; 
 
(c) the details of funds required for execution of the said two projects; and 
 
(d) the details of the steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to pool funds 
for the above projects? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a)  The National Culture Fund (NCF) has identified approximately 250 heritage 
conservation projects and showcased them on its website for mobilization of voluntary 
contributions under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and other philanthropic 
initiatives.  The projects relating to (i) removal and resetting of approach steps to the Hill Fort 
at Udayagiri and (ii) removal and resetting of ancient flooring inside the Ranganayakula 
temple in Udayagiri, in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh, are also among them. 
 
(b) The projects are displayed on the NCF website to facilitate support from prospective 
CSR donors and other philanthropists. Their implementation is dependent upon the interest 
and willingness of prospective donors to support the projects. As on date, no CSR donor has 
confirmed financial support for these two projects. 
 
(c) The estimated cost for the execution of the said two projects is Rs.7.25 crores. 
However, the final scope and cost of each project may vary depending upon the requirements 
of the donor and the technical assessment of the Archaeological Survey of India. 
  
(d) To mobilize resources, NCF hosts project details on its portal to enable prospective 
donors to identify projects based on location, heritage significance, thematic interest and level 
of financial commitment. However, NCF is open to accept CSR contributions and donations 
from donors for work required at other monuments also, as per the interest and willingness of 
the donor.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2451 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
Protection of Existing Natural Forests 
 
2451. THIRU DR. S JAGATHRATCHAKAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed scientific findings relating to tropical forest 
regeneration indicating that although tree cover may return relatively quickly after 
deforestation, full biodiversity recovery, restoration of ecological functions and revival 
of wildlife habitats require substantially longer periods;  
(b) if so, the details of measures undertaken by the Government to strengthen protection of 
existing natural forests, improve ecological restoration programmes, conserve native 
flora and fauna and enhance monitoring of forest ecosystem health across the country; 
and; 
(c)  the initiatives proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure that afforestation 
efforts prioritize biodiversity restoration, ecosystem integrity and long-term ecological 
resilience, promote the use of indigenous species and reduce reliance on plantation-
focused targets while supporting sustainable conservation outcomes across the 
country? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (c) Scientific evidence indicates that while tree cover may recover through 
natural regeneration and afforestation, restoration of biodiversity, ecological 
functions and wildlife habitats is a gradual process that depends on local 
ecological conditions and appropriate management interventions. The 
conservation of natural forests and restoration of degraded forest landscapes 
is carried out through assisted natural regeneration, artificial regeneration, 
compensatory afforestation under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) 
Adhiniyam, 1980 and the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, as 
well as through programmes such as the Green India Mission, Nagar Van 
Yojana, Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline habitats and Tangible Incomes 
(MISHTI) and other afforestation and restoration initiatives. These 
interventions are implemented in accordance with the objectives and 
guidelines of the respective Acts and programmes, which include restoration 
of degraded forest landscapes, plantation of suitable indigenous/native 
species and biodiversity conservation, as applicable. 
The National Working Plan Code-2023 lays down guidelines for sustainable 

forest management, including biodiversity conservation, restoration of 
degraded forests, wildlife habitat improvement, soil and water conservation 
and site-specific silvicultural practices. Forest and tree cover are monitored 
periodically by the Forest Survey of India through the India State of Forest 
Report, while biodiversity conservation is supported through the Protected 
Area network and other conservation measures implemented by the Central 
and State Governments. 
  *****

entries.t: Establishment of Foreign Universities Campuses in India
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2452 
ANSWERED ON 03/08/2026 
 
Establishment of Foreign Universities Campuses in India 
 
2452. Shri Appalanaidu Kalisetti: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the number of foreign universities that have applied to establish campuses in India under 
the University Grants Commission (UGC) guidelines, State-wise, with specific details for 
Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) the present status of these applications, including the number of institutions granted 
approval and issued letters of intent, with particular reference to Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) the proposed academic infrastructure and programmes to be offered by such foreign 
universities in India; 
(d) the details of any Government funding provided to support the establishment of these 
foreign campuses, State-wise, including funds allocated to Andhra Pradesh; and  
(e) the oversight and monitoring mechanism prescribed under the UGC guidelines for 
regulating such foreign university campuses, including those proposed in Andhra Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e): A number of Foreign Higher Educational Institutions (FHEIs) have expressed interests 
to establish their branch campuses in India, under the University Grants Commission (UGC) 
(Setting up and Operation of Campuses of Foreign Higher Educational Institutions in India) 
Regulations 2023. 
UGC has issued 16 Letters of Intent (LoIs) to 15 FHEIs from Australia, Italy, United Kingdom 
and United State of America (USA) to establish their campuses at various places in India including 
Bengaluru, Greater Noida, Gurugram, Mumbai and Chennai. The FHEIs proposing to open branch 
campuses in India have indicated to run programmes in business, economics, accounting, finance, 
software engineering, data science, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, game design, 

entrepreneurship, innovation, biomedical sciences, among other emerging fields to meet global 
academic and industry demands. 
 
UGC has instituted a single-window clearance mechanism and constituted a high-powered 
Standing Committee to evaluate the proposals for establishment of FHEI campuses in India. The 
Committee examines the applications and makes recommendations to the Commission. Based on 
these recommendations, UGC grants in-principle approval and issues a Letter of Intent. Only 
FHEIs ranked within the top 500 globally ranked universities are eligible, and applicants must 
submit the latest accreditation or quality assurance reports from recognized bodies. 
 
UGC regulatory framework is designed to ensure that the education imparted in India is of the 
same standard as that offered at the parent campus abroad, while also ensuring compliance with 
applicable laws and regulations in India. The qualifications awarded by FHEIs under the UGC 
Regulations shall be recognized and treated as equivalent to any corresponding qualification 
awarded by Indian Higher Educational Institutions, and no further equivalence from any authority 
would be required.  
 
Further, the government has also constituted a ‘Facilitation Committee for FHEIs’ on 16th 
December 2025. The Committee is mandated to assist the FHEIs in establishment of their 
campuses in India, after the hand-over of the LoI by UGC. The Committee also oversees and 
monitors the academic/financial/governance etc. related aspects vis-à-vis the regulatory 
mechanisms in India.  
*****

entries.t: Violation of Labour Laws by IT Companies
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2453 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
VIOLATION OF LABOUR LAWS BY IT COMPANIES 
 
2453. ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the Government is aware of the violation of Labour Laws by 
IT Companies by mass termination of employees without prior notice 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)whether the Govern ment has any plan to implement regulatory 
measures to address the violation of labour laws by the IT companies; 
and 
(c)if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (c): “Labour” as a subject falls in the Concurrent List. Based on 
their respective jurisdiction as demarcated in the Industrial Relations 
Code, 2020, Central and State Governments take actions to address the 
issues of the workers and protect their interests.  In the establishments 
that lie in the jurisdiction of Central Government, the Central Industial 
Relations Machinery (CIRM) is entrusted with the task of maintaining 
good industrial relations and protecting the interest of workers including 
in matters relating to t ermination, retrenchment or lay -off and its 
prevention. The data pertaining to the private sector are maintained by 
the respective State Governments. 
  The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 contains various 
provisions to safeguard workers' rights and job sec urity, including 
statutory safeguards in the form of mandatory notice period, 
retrenchment compensation and provision for retrenched workers to be 
given preference in re -employment are applicable for all retrenched 
workers. The Code also introduces Workers Re-skilling fund for training 
of retrenched workers for the first time with a view to providing financial 
support to retrenched workers to utilize that amount for his re -skilling. 
The Negotiating Unions/Negotiating Councils have been brought under 
the statutory provisions to strengthen collective bargaining.  
  Further, the industrial establishments having 300 or more 
workers are required to seek prior permission of the appropriate 
government for lay-off, retrenchment and closure.  
*****

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY

ANSWERED ON- 03.08.2026 
 
Nutrition Equivalence in PM POSHAN Substitutions 
 
2454. Shri Azad Kirti Jha: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has prescribed a nutrition -equivalence protocol before eggs or  other 
protein-rich food items are replaced under PM POSHAN, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether such protocol considers protein quality, bio -availability, micronutrient density, cost per 
child, local acceptability and supply reliability, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the number of States and districts where such substitution was permitted during the last five years 
and the current year; 
 
(d) whether substitution was permitted in any case without a recorded nutrition assessment; and 
 
(e) if so, the reasons therefor and the corrective steps taken thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (e): Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most of the Government 
Schools and School Boards are under the administration of the State Government  and Union 
Territory (UT) Administrations. PM POSHAN Scheme is implemented in partnership with the State 
Governments and UT Administrations. The overall responsibility for providing hot and nutritious 
meal to all children studying in Bal Vatika (just before class 1) and classes I to VIII of Government 
and Government aided schools lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations. The States 
and UTs are encouraged to decide menu suitable to the local conditions within the prescribed 
nutrition and food norms and to procure locally grown food item s like millets, vegetables, 
condiments etc.  
 
  

Under the PM Poshan Scheme, one hot cooked meal is provided to all eligible children on all 
school working days. As per the provisions of National Food Security Act, 2013 and the Guidelines 
of the Scheme, the nutritional and food norms prescribed under the Scheme are as follows:

undertaken in accordance with the approved Management Plan/Tiger 
Conservation Plan/ Working Plan as applicable. The details of death of wild 
animals are maintained at the level of States/Union Territories. Incidents of 
mass mortality or distress due to extreme heat condition have not been reported 
by the States/ Union Territories. 
 
The important measures taken by Government for protection of wildlife, 
including from those attributed to heatwaves, include: 
 
i.  A network of Protected Areas have been created in the country for 
protection and conservation of wildlife and its habitat. 
ii. This Ministry has issued guidelines for preparation of Management 
Plans, in accordance with Section 33 of the Wild Life (Protection) 
Act, 1972. The guidelines has a provision for integrating climate 
change adaptation in management planning of Protected Areas. 
iii. Financial assistance is provided to State Governments /Union 
Territory Administrations for management of wildlife and 
development of its habitat under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes 

‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’ and ‘Project Tiger & Elephant’. 
The activities supported under the scheme include for augmentation 
of water supply, creation and maintenance of water harvesting/ 
retention structures like bunds, tanks, wells, check dams, ponds, 
streams etc. 
 
iv. This Ministry has issued an advisory to States/Union Territories, to 
enhance preparedness for wildlife, zoos and allied sectors in view of 
ensuing heat wave and flood seasons. 
v. Technology like Camera traps, drones, wireless, e-surveillance, 
early warning systems etc. are used for monitoring of wild animals, 
to manage the human wildlife conflict.

QUESTION 
2457. Shri Sasikanth Senthil: 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) expenditure by companies during 
each of the last three years, along with the amount remaining unspent or 
transferred to the Unspent CSR Account; 
 
(b) the details of CSR expenditure during the said period, State/UT -wise; 
 
(c) whether  CSR spending is concentrated in a few States while some States 
receive comparatively low amounts, if so, the details of the reasons therefor; and  
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to encourage a more balanced and equitable 
regional distribution of CSR funds, particularly in underserved and backward areas?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS   AND MINISTER 
OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a) & (b):  Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 provides for treatment of 
unspent CSR amount. In the case of an ongoing project, the company is required 
to transfer the unspent amount to a special account of the company i.e ‘Unspent 
CSR Account’, within 30 days fro m the end of financial year and spend the same 
in pursuance of its CSR policy within the next three financial years from the date 
of such transfer. After the lapse of three financial years, the amount remaining 
unspent, if any, is required to be transferre d to any Fund mentioned in Schedule 
VII of the Act within a period of thirty days from the date of completion of the third 
financial year. In case of other than an ongoing project, the company is required 
to transfer the unspent CSR amount to any Fund mentioned in Schedule VII of the 
Act within a period of six months from the end of the financial year.  On the basis 
of annual filings made by companies in the MCA21 registry, state-wise CSR 
expenditure by the companies during the last three Financial Years i. e. FY 2022-
23 to FY 2024 -25 is attached at Annexure. The data of unspent CSR account of 
Companies is not maintained centrally. 
Contd….2/ 
 
 
 
 

 
 
-2- 
(c) & (d):  Under the Companies Act, 2013, CSR is a Board driven process and the 
Board of the company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR 
activities of the company based on the recommendation of its CSR Committee. 
The first proviso to Section 135 (5) of the Act provides that the company shall give 
preference to the local area and areas aroun d it where it operates. However, the 
emphasis on local area is only directory and not mandatory in nature and 
companies need to balance local area preference with national priorities. The 
Government does not mandate the companies to spend in any particular  
geographical area or for any particular activity.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-2458  
ANSWERED ON-03/08/2026 
 
Strengthening Higher Education for Emerging Technologies 
 
2458. Thiru D M Kathir Anand: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the roadmap prepared by the Government to modernise higher education in view of the rapid advancement 
of Artificial Intelligence (AI), with emphasis on flexible learning pathways, continuous skill development, 
experiential education and knowledge creation through research; 
(b) the approach adopted by the Government to encourage universities and higher educational institutions to 
strengthen project-based learning, industry collaboration, innovation, entrepreneurship and li felong learning 
alongside conventional academic programmes; 
(c) the assistance provided for redesigning curricula to equip students with future -ready competencies in 
emerging technologies and digital applications; 
(d) the collaboration with academic institutions, industry, research organisations and regulatory bodies for 
promoting responsible integration of Artificial Intelligence in higher education; and 
(e) whether any proposals are under consideration by the Government for building an education eco system 
that remains relevant to changing technologies, evolving employment patterns and national development 
priorities and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e): Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with an aim for holistic 
development of students. NEP 2020  lays emphasis on  multidisciplinarity, imaginative & flexible curricular 
structures, integration of skills and recommends that the pedagogy must evolve to make education more 
experiential, inquiry-driven, discovery-oriented, and learner-centred. 
In line with the vision of NEP 2020, the Government has issued key guidelines and taken several initiatives to 
upgrade curricula, pedagogy, and develop digital infrastructure in order to create future-ready talent pipeline. 
 
To upgrade the higher education curricula, the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) has revised 
its Model Curricula with inputs from industry experts by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science 
(DS), Machine Learning (ML), Cyber Security, Robotics, Quantum Computing, and other emerging 
technologies across technical disciplines. During the year 2025–26, more than 2100 AICTE -approved 
institutions offered courses in AI & other emerging area, with an approved intake of more than 2.80 lakh 
students. 

To enhance employability of the students and achieve the objectives of NEP 2020, the National Credit 
Framework (NCrF) has been issued, enabling integration o f skill education into academia. The NCrF has a 
provision for the accumulation of a maximum of 50% of the total credit required through skill-based courses. 
Further, the University Grants Commission has issued “Guidelines on Sustainable and Vibrant Univers ity-
Industry Linkage System for Indian Universities” to promote Research & Development and develop the skill 
sets amongst the learners and make them industry ready. Further, AICTE’s Approval Process Handbook 2024-
25 to 2026-27 has “Essential and Desirable Requirements for Technical Institutions”, which include Institute-
Industry Cell, establishment of Institution ’s Innovation Council  and compulsory i nternship for final year 
students as essential requirements for approval.  
 
Additionally, UGC has introduced “Guidelines for Internship/Research Internship for Under Graduate 
Students”, with an aim to improve employability, develop interest for research and provide exposure to 
emerging technologies. Further, UGC has also formulated the “UGC Guidelines for Higher Educational 
Institutions to Offer Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP) ” to embed the competencies 
required by the industry in the university curriculum. 
 
The Ministry of Education implements the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) to impart on-
the-job training  in collaboration with industry  to enhance the employability of youth. To meet the rising 
demand for AI talent, the Ministry has launched the AI Apprenticeship Programme under NA TS. This initiative 
aims to develop expertise in various areas such as Data Science, Machine Learning, Application Development, 
Prompt Engineering, etc for graduates, diploma holders, AEDP students. Till date, more than 75000 
apprentices have benefited from the AI Apprenticeship Programme. 
 
To leverage the potential of Information and Communication Technology, Minis try of Education is 
implementing the National Mission on Education through ICT (NMEICT). Under the NMEICT scheme Study 
Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM) platform has been launched to promote 
lifelong learning through free courses by premier

entries.t: Regulation of Private Coaching Centres in Tamil Nadu
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2459 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
Regulation of Private Coaching Centres in Tamil Nadu 
2459. Shri Mani A: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the functioning and regulation of private 
competitive examination coaching  centres in Tamil Nadu, if so, the details thereof, including the 
measures proposed to ensure transparency in fee structures, quality of teaching, student safety and 
accountability; 
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to strengthen access to affordable and high -quality coaching 
support for students from rural and educationally backward districts of Tamil Nadu, includ ing 
Dharmapuri, through digital learning platforms, school -based mentoring and Government -supported 
coaching initiatives, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government has received complaints regarding excessive academic pressure, 
misleading advertisements, unfair practices, inadequate student welfare measures or other irregularities 
in coaching centres operating in Tamil Nadu during the last three years, if so, the details thereof and 
the action taken thereon; and 
 
(d) the steps taken/proposed to  be taken by the Government to ensure equitable access to quality 
coaching and career guidance for students belonging to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), 
Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and other disadvantaged communities in Tamil Nadu? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a): Keeping in view the growth in number of unregulated private coaching centres; instances of such 
centers charging exorbitant fees from students; loss of precious lives due to fire and other accidents ; 
significance of mental well-being; and many malpractices being adopted by these centres, Ministry has 
circulated Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Center to States/UTs on 16.01.2024 for taking further 
action by way of appro priate legal framework. The guidelines for regulation of coaching centres are 
accessible at https://www.dohe-education.gov.in/documents/acts-and-policies/guidelines-for-
regulation-of-coaching-center-ADNyE DOtQWa?pageTitle=Guidelines-for-Regulation-of-Coaching-
Center  
 

The Guidelines encompass several key aspects, incl uding specifying conditions and necessary 
documents for registration, issues related to fees, outlining infrastructure prerequisites for establishing 
coaching centers, establishing a code of conduct for coaching centers; lay emphasis on significance of 
mental well -being, no batch segregation , maintenance of records , grievance/complaint redressal 
mechanism etc. The guidelines inter-alia provide for coaching center to have a website with updated 
details of the qualification of tutors, details and duration of courses/curriculum, the fees being charged, 
easy exit policy, fee refund policy, number of students undertaken coaching from the center and 
number of students finally succeeded in getting admission in Higher Education Institutions etc. 
Several States/UTs have brought out guidelines / regulations / legislations to regulate the Private 
Coaching and tuition classes in their respective States/UTs. State Government of Tamil Nadu has also 
released Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centres, 20 26, which provide a 
comprehensive framework to ensure transparency, quality, student safety, and accountability in the 
functioning of coaching centres. The guidelines mandate transparent disclosure of fee structures, 
refund and exit policies, and other key information through websites and prospectuses. Guidelines also 
prescribe minimum educational qualifications for teachers, prohibit misleading claims , require 
counselling support and mental health sensitisation of teachers , mandatory structural and fire safet y 
certifications, adequate sanitation, CCTV surveillance, first -aid facilities, emergency preparedness, 
and grievance redressal mechanisms . Further, the Guidelines strengthen accountability by requiring 
compulsory registration, periodic inspections, maintenance of records, annual reporting, and penalties, 
including cancellation of registration, for non-compliance. 
(b): Education is subject of concurrent list and both Central and State government work collaboratively 
to provide equitable access to education.  Centre, various State and UT governments are providing  
remedial classes to students for competitive exams. SATHEE is one such initiative of Central  
government, launched in November, 2023, to provide free of cost high -quality content for the  
competitive examinations like JEE and NEET, along with providing an online assessment module  
for students. It leverages Web Platform, Mobile Application, YouTube live sessions & DTH channels 
for delivery. More than 15,000 + multilingual video lectures

2460. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:- 
(a) the number of financial fraud cases involving banking, digital payments and other financial  
transactions reported during last three financial years, year-wise, category-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(b) the total amount involved in such cases and the amount frozen, recovered and refunded to  victims, 
year-wise, category-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number of victims whose defrauded amounts were fully or partially recovered and refunded during 
the said period, year-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(d) the mechanisms for recovery of defrauded amounts and restitution to victims, including  agencies 
responsible for coordination and timelines prescribed for recovery and refund; 
(e) whether the Government has assessed the recovery and refund rates in financial fraud cases, if so, the 
details thereof along with the reasons for non-recovery or delay in restitution to victims; and 
(f) the steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government to strengthen real -time fraud detection, 
inter-bank and inter-agency coordination, recovery of defrauded amounts and time -bound restitution to 
victims? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (c): Category -wise and State/UT -wise details of frauds  reported by Scheduled Commercial Banks  
(excluding Regional Rural Banks) and All India Financial Institutions for the last three financial years (FYs) 
are at Annex-1 and Annex-2 respectively. 
Further, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has apprised that the details of amount frozen, recovered and 
refunded to the victims are not maintained by it. 
(d) to (f): In terms of the RBI’s Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks and 
All India Financial Institutions, banks are required to immediately report the incidents of fraud to different 
Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), viz.  State/UT Police, Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), 
Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), depending on the amount involved in the fraud.  Since the 
complexity of the fraud cases are unique and multiple agencies/institutions/tribunals/courts are involved, 
there are no defined timelines for recovery of amount involved in frauds. Attempts are made by all the 
agencies involved to recover and resolve at the earliest.  

(i) An online searchable database of frauds reported by banks, in the form of Central Fraud Registry, 
has been set up by the RBI to enable timely identification, control and mitigation of fraud risk. 
(iv) RBI has launched an Artificial Intelligence (AI) based tool ‘MuleHunter’ for identification of 
money mule and advised the banks and financial institutions for its uses. 
(v) Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) has been incorporated to detect, prevent, 
and analyse fraud in rapidly expanding digital payments ecosystem in real time by leveraging 
cutting-edge technologies, including AI/ML and Big Data Analytics. 
(vi) Several initiatives have been taken to spread awareness amongst customers, which inter alia include, 
dissemination of messages on cybercrime through short message service (SMS), radio campaigns, 
publicity on prevention of cybercrime and cyber safety tips through social media accounts of I4C, 
conducting of electronic-banking awareness and training (e-BAAT) programmes by RBI. 
 
***** 
 
Details of recovery and refund in fraud cases is as per Annex-1. Further, recovery in fraud loans is an 
ongoing process and banks initiate recovery actions under various recovery mechanisms available to them, 
which include, inter alia, filing of suits in civil courts or in Debt Recovery Tribunals, action under the 
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforc ement of Security Interest Act, filing of 
cases in the National Company Law Tribunal under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.  
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has established the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) 
to provide a comprehensive ecosystem for LEAs to deal with cybercrime. Under this framework, the 
National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP) serves as the primary public interface, enabling citizens to 
report all cyber offences, including cyber-enabled financial crimes.

into the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS). The CFCFRMS

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2461

Environmental Clearance to Shree Cement Limited 
 
2461. SHRI VIJAY BAGHEL: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) whether Shree Cement Limited, Khapradih, Chhattisgarh was granted Environmental 
Clearance on 11.09.2019 for a clinker production capacity of 13.5 MTPA at a time when the 
available limestone linkage was not commensurate with the approved capacity if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b) whether the company stated before the Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board that 
the 13.5 MTPA capacity had been commissioned, while subsequently, in its application to the 
Ministry for Unit-IV, it stated that the previously approved capacity had not been fully installed, 
if so, whether these installed contradictory records have been examined and if so, the details in 
this regard; and 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to conduct an independent inquiry into the limestone 
linkage, actual production, environmental compliance and the potential impact on State revenue 
in respect of the said project, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c): 
An Environment Clearance (EC) was granted by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and 
Climate Change (MoEFCC) on 11-09-2019 to M/s Shree Raipur Cement Plant (a unit of 
M/s Shree Cement Limited) in respect of a project located near Village Khapradih, Tehsil 
Simga, District Balodabazar – Bhatapara, Chhattisgarh. The EC was accorded for 
expansion in production of clinker manufacturing from 5.2 Million Tonnes Per Annum 
(MTPA) to 13.5 MTPA and cement manufacturing from 6 MTPA to 16.5 MTPA, along 
with Waste Heat Recovery Power Plant from 15 to 30 MW, Captive Power Plant from 
25 MW to 125 MW and Synthetic Gypsum Unit of 65 Tons per Hour. As per the 
submission made by the Project Proponent (PP), the proposed expansion involved 
enhancement of production in existing Units 1 and 2, and setting up of new Unit-3 in a 
phase-wise manner. The proposed enhancement in production was linked to the proposed 

expansion of Bharuwadih - Samradih and Karhi - Chandi limestone mines for which PP 
had already applied for grant of the EC. In light of the proposed linkage of mines, an EC 
condition was also prescribed as below: 
“The limestone for the project shall be sourced only from (i) Existing Captive 
Semradih & Bharuwadih Limestone (M.L Area 531.126 ha) and (ii) Karhi - 
Chandi Limestone Mine (ML area 242.127 ha) which are located adjacent to 
plant site. In case of any change in source of limestone, the project proponent 
shall obtain prior permission from MoEF&CC.” 
 
After due examination, the Ministry accorded ECs to the Bharuwadih - Samradih and 
Karhi - Chandi limestone mines on 27-08-2020 and 15-05-2020 for limestone 
production of 11.06 MTPA and 1.5 MTPA, respectively. As per the EIA reports 
submitted by the Project Proponent, the limestone requirement of the cement plant is 
proposed to be met from these two mines. As on date, no application for grant of EC 
pertaining to Unit-4 is pending with the Ministry. 
 
The Sub Office, Raipur had submitted Certified Compliance Report (CCR) vide letter 
dated 10-09-2025. The environmental compliance status of the project has been 
examined, as per the standard operating procedure (SoP) of the Ministry, with respect 
to the ECs associated with the project, including EC dated 11.09.2019 and it has been 
concluded that no major violation of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 has been 
observed, prima facie for the cement plant operations.  
 
As per the information provided by the Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board, 
it had granted Consent to Operate to M/s Shree Cement Limited, Village-Khapradih, 
Tehsil - Simga, District - Balodabazar-Bhatapara (C.G.) for total clinker production 
capacity of 12.5 MTPA against EC permitted clinker capacity of 13.5 MTPA. Cement 
plant of M/s Shree Cement Limited, Village- Khapradih, Tehsil - Simga, District - 
Balodabazar-Bhatapara (C.G.) was inspected by the Chhattisgarh Environment 
Conservation Board on 06-03-2026. During inspection, industry was found operational 
and the pollution control systems such as ESPs and bag filters are in operation. The 
STP/ETP installed for treated wastewater was also found to be operational.

 Under the component ‘ Creation and Up -gradation of Sports

2464. DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of the expansion of banking services in rural areas under the financial 
inclusion programme in the country; 
(b) the steps being taken by the Government to increase the number of bank branches and 
ATMs in rural areas; 
(c) the current status of accounts opened under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY); 
(d) the measures being taken by the Government to ensure transparency and timely 
disbursement of agricultural credit; and 
(e) the action plan of the Government to strengthen digital banking and cybersecurity? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) As per the data uploaded by banks on Jan Dhan Darshak (JDD) App., the country has 
achieved near-universal banking coverage, with 99.92% of inhabited villages (6,00,868 out of 
6,01,328) now served by a banking outlet (Bank branch / Business Correspondent / India Post 
Payments Bank (IPPB)) within a radius of 5 km. This banking expansion is support ed by a 
robust infrastructure of over 1.81 lakh bank branches, 17.36 lakh Business Correspondents 
(BCs), and 1.65 lakh IPPB centres, as on 17.07.2026. 
 
(b) To ensure accessibility of banking services in rural and remote areas, the endeavour of the 
Government is to provide a banking outlet (Bank branch / Business Correspondent / India Post 
Payments Bank) within 5 kilometres radius of all inhabited villages in the country.  
Further, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has permitted Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, 
Payments Banks, Local Area Banks and Regional Rural Banks, to open bank branches 
anywhere in India without prior approval, provided 25% are in unbanked rural areas. 
 
Moreover, in pursuance of extant RBI guidelines, rolling out of banking outlets in unc overed 
areas is a continuous process looked after by the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) / 
Union Territory Level Bankers Committee (UTLBC), in consultation with the concerned 
State/UT Government, member Banks and other stakeholders. Banks, inter -alia, consider 
proposals for opening banking outlets in the light of RBI’s instructions, their business plans 
and their commercial viability.  
 

(c) As on 17.07.2026, there are a total number of 58.77 crore PMJDY accounts in the country, 
having a balance of ₹ 3,12,414 Crore. 
 
(d) Various steps have been taken by the Government to ensure transparency and timely 
disbursement of agriculture credit, inter – alia include: 
i. The Jan Samarth Portal has been started as a one -stop digital platform for linking 
Government-Sponsored loans and subsidies schemes. It provides a quick and efficient 
way to apply for loans and their timely sanction based on a digital evaluation of the 
applicant’s data. 
ii. To streamline the agricultural credit delivery process various digital initiative s have 
been introduced. These include the e -KYC application developed by NABARD, 
KRISHIKA by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, and similar digital 
applications development by banks to support beneficiary identification, outreach, loan 
application processing and monitoring. 
iii. Kisan Rin Portal (KRP) has been launched by Department of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare in September 2023, enabling Aadhaar-based beneficiary verification and faster 
digital claim settlements under the Modified Interest  Subvention Scheme (MISS) for 
loans availed through KCC. 
 
(e) The Government and RBI have been taking up various initiatives from time to time to 
strengthen cyber security of digital payment transaction and protect citizens from cyber 
financial frauds. This inter-alia, includes: 
i. The government in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India has set up India Digital 
Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC) to share real -time fraud intelligence and 
alerts to the banks and financial institutions by leveraging advanced technologies such 
as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Big Data Analytics. 
ii. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued Master Directions on Digital Payment Security 
Controls in February, 2021 to combat web and mobile app threats. These guidelines 
mandate the banks to implement a common minimum standards of security controls for 
various payment channels like internet, mobile banking, card payment etc. 
iii. RBI has launched an Artificial Intelligence (AI) based tool ‘MuleHunter’ for 
identification of money mule and advised the banks and financial institutions for its 
uses.  
iv. Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has 
been proactively analysing the digital lending apps. In order to facilitate the citizens to 
report cyber incidents including fa

PM Mudra Yojana 
 
†2466. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA: 
 
 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the current status of the implementation of Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana along with the details of the 
number and amount of loans sanctioned and disbursed under the scheme so far in Rajasthan, year-wise 
and district-wise including Jhunjhunu district;  
(b) whether the Government has carried out any review/evaluat ion of the effectiveness of the scheme; 
(c) if so, the major findings thereof and the steps taken for improvement and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether it is a fact that the said scheme has remained c onfined only to figures in some areas without 
reaching the actual beneficiaries, if so, the details thereof;  
(e) whether it is also a fact that despite genuine need, many el igible applicants hav e not been sanctioned 
loans under the said scheme by banks, if so, the reasons therefor;  
(f) whether the complaints regarding denial of loans/unnec essary delay by banks have been received; and 
(g) if so, the details of such cases and their disposal du ring last five years along with Parliamentary 
Constituency-wise details including the Jhunjhunu Lok Sabha Constituency in Rajasthan, year-wise ? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FIN ANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (g ):  As on June, 2026 , more than 59.14 crore loans, have been sanctioned/disbursed  under the 
Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), since launch of the Scheme.  
The number and amount of loans sanctioned/ disbursed under PMMY in the State of Rajasthan, 
year/district-wise including Jhunjhunu District is placed at Annexure I. 
The Government has undertaken two assessments of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) since 
its inception through the Ministry of Labour and Employment in 2018 and NITI Aayog in 2023. The 
details of which are as under: 
(i)  Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) - A large sample survey was conducted at the national 
level to estimate employment generation under PMMY.  As per the survey results, PMMY helped in 

generation of 1.12 crore net additional employment during a period of approximately 3 years (i.e. from 
2015 to 2018); and   
(ii)  NITI Aayog evaluated the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Scheme in November 2023 which , inter-alia, 
state that :  
a) the small entrepreneurs got  easy access to micro credit at gross root level;  
b) it helped the individuals and sole proprietors to avail the loan across geographies;  
c) attracted first-time entrepreneurs and helped them to graduate to higher categories of loans.        
Government has taken various steps towards e ffective implementation of the S cheme. These, inter -alia, 
include publicity campaigns, simplification of application form, Credit Guarantee Scheme, nomination of 
Mudra Nodal Officer promoting digital proce ss for banks and frequent reviews at various levels by 
Government and Banks to monitor the achievement under the scheme. 
 
As per RBI circular dated 9th April, 2010, all credit related matters of banks including sanction or decline 
of loans are governed by the bank’s own lending policies  approved by the Board , subject to extant 
guidelines of RBI. 
Citizens can approach banks through online portals and customer care numbers for any assistance to 
directly address their issues to the concerned bank branches. Further, the Board of Directors of individual 
banks lay down appropriate grievance redressal mechanisms within the organization to resolve customer 
grievances. If grievances involving deficiency in services rendered by entities regulated by RBI are not 
resolved to the satisfaction of the customers or not replied to within a period of 30 days by the regulated 
entity, the customer can approach the “Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021” that 
provides cost -free redressal of complaints. Government of In dia also hosts a web -based portal i.e. 
Centralized Public Grievance Redressal and Monitoring System (CPGRAM) wherein Citizens can file 
their grievances relating to Ministries/Departments of Government of India of States/UTs.  
The detail of complaints received regarding denial of loans/ unnecessary delay by banks is not maintained 
centrally.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
   UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2467 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT AND PROFESSIONAL MANAGEMENT  
OF HERITAGE DESTINATIONS  
 
2467. SHRI VISHNU DATT SHARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is promoting development and professional 
management of major heritage destinations across the country, 
particularly UNESCO World Heritage Sites and iconic tourist 
destinations;  
(b) whether Khajuraho, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, one of the 
country’s recognised iconic tourist destinations and due to its 
historical and cultural significance, has been considered for 
establishment of a dedicated tourism office to coordinate tourism 
development and facilitate visitors; 
(c)  whether the Government is cognizant that the existing Light and Sound 
Show at the Khajuraho temple complex requires reconceptualization 
and technological upgradation;  
(d)  if so, the details of efforts being made to upgrade the Light and Sound 
Show and improve visitor experience; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM            (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a): Identification, promotion and development of tourism infrastructure, 
amenities and experiences at tourist destinations including places of 
historical, heritage and iconic significance are primarily undertaken by the 
concerned State Government/UT Administration. However, the Ministry of 
Tourism, under its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development 
(CBDD), and Pilgrimage  Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation 
Drive (PRASHAD), provides financial assistance for the development of 

tourism related infrastructure and experiences across the country, 
including those in the State of Madhya Pradesh.  
 
The details of projects sanctioned under the aforementioned schemes  by 
the Ministry of Tourism  in the State of Madhya Pradesh, is given in the 
Annexure. 
 
Also, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), undertake, conservation, 
preservation and maintenance of monuments and sites declared protected 
under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 
1958. 
 
Further, ASI provide amenities for visitors in the protected 
monuments/sites including those listed as World Heritage Properties. While 
ensuring a good state of preservation, ASI is committed to offering requisite 
amenities at protected monuments/ sites, s ubject to feasibility. The 
amenities include washrooms, drinking water, child care room, benches, 
pathways, garbage bins, signage, Sound & Light shows, illumination, 
souvenir shop, interpretation center, cafeteria, etc. 
 
ASI receives developmental proposal from various stakeholders 
including various ministries/departments of union/state governments under 
various centre or state-run scheme/project/program.  
 
Additionally, ASI launched the Adopt A Heritage 2.0 program, 
exclusively for protected monuments of national importance, to create a 
framework for engagement with private/public sector companies and NGOs/ 
Trusts/ Societies, etc., develop/provide a group of  amenities at protected 
monuments to enhance visitors' experience and make them visitor-friendly. 
 
(b): As far as establishment of a dedicated tourism office to coordinate 
tourism development and facilitate visitors is concerned no proposal is 
currently under consideration for establishing an office at Khajuraho. 
However, the Ministry of Tourism has an India  Tourism Office at Indore, 
Madhya Pradesh. 
 
(c) to (e): At present, no proposal specific to the development/upgradation 
of Light and Sound Show at the Khajuraho temple complex is under 
consideration in the Ministry of Tourism.  
 
Receiving proposals for tourism infrastructure development is a 
continuous process. The Proposals for seeking financial assistance for the 
development of the tourism infrastructure are formulated by the concerned 

States and UTs. The proposals received are examined in accordance with 
the prescribed guidelines, and financial assistance is provided subject to 
fulfilment of the stipulated conditions and availability of funds. 
 
Further, as informed by ASI the Sound and Light show at the Western 
Group of Temples, Khajuraho is operated by the Department of Tourism, 
Government of Madhya Pradesh (MP). The same has been upgraded recently 
by them installing the laser beam light, high digital volume sound system 
and other ancillary technical components.

relating to Artificial Intelligence (AI), dro nes, robotics, cyber security, data analytics, green 
technology and other emerging fields extensively into higher education and to regularly update 
the curricula in accordance with industry requirements, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c): The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 promotes holistic, multidisciplinary and 
flexible higher education, enabling students to acquire knowledge and skills beyond a single 
discipline and pursue diverse educational and professional pathways. It envisage s integration 
of vocational education into undergraduate and graduate programs. In line with (NEP), 2020, 
various measures have been taken to integrate skill development and vocational education with 
regular academic programmes in Higher Educational Instit utions (HEIs). The National Credit 
Framework (NCrF), National Higher Education Qualifications Framework (NHEQF), 
Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and Multiple Entry and Multiple Exit provisions provide for 
integration, accumulation and transfer of academic, vocational and experiential learning. The 
University Grant Commission (UGC) has supported skill-based education through Community 
Colleges, B.Voc. Degree Programmes and Deen Dayal Upadhyay Centres for Knowledge 
Acquisition and Upgradation of Skilled Human Abilities and Livelihood. The All India Council 
for Technical Education (AICTE) and UGC have issued guidelines for Apprenticeship 
Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP), 2025 for higher education programmes under their 
respective domains. National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) is implemented by the 
Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education through four regional Boards of 
Apprenticeship Training/Practical Training (BoATs/BoPT) located at Mumbai, Kanpur, 

Chennai and Kolkata. The scheme aims at providing on-the-job training and skilling of Indian 
youth. It provides apprenticeship training to Graduates / Diploma holders within the five years 
of completion of their courses and to the students of Apprenticeship Embedded Degree 
Programmes (AEDP). Under NATS, till date ~457 MOUs have been signed with HEIs for 
AEDP implementation. 
 
Under the Approval Process Handbook (APH) 2024 –2027, AICTE -approved existing 
institutions are permitted to conduct Vocational and Industrial Training Institute (ITI) courses 
by using their existing infrastructure, subject to the applicable provisions of the APH. Skill 
Universities are facilitating the integration of vocational education with higher education. Five 
Skill Universities have been recognised by NCVET (National Council for vocational Education 
and Training) as Awarding Bodies. This enables them to offer NSQF -aligned qualifications, 
award nationally recognised skill certificates and implement credit -based pathways under the 
National Credit Framework (NCrF), thereby promoting seamless mobility between vocational 
and higher education.  
 
AICTE-approved programmes provide for mandatory internships, industrial training, project 
work and experiential learning. AICTE has promoted Industry -Institute Interaction through 
Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with industries and organisations for curriculum 
development, faculty training, internships, innovation and entrepreneurship. Further, 424 
AICTE IDEA Labs have been established to promote experiential learning, innovation, design 
thinking and product development. The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) ecosystem has 
also been strengthened to promote innovation, entrepreneurship and start -up culture. 
Apprenticeship opportunities have been promoted through collaboration with indus tries and 
support for apprenticeship -integrated degree programmes. Credit -based skill courses aligned 
with the NCrF and ABC provide flexible learning pathways. UGC has enabled Universities to 
adopt skill based micro -credentials as a part of their cu

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2471 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
REVIEW AND IMPLEMENTATION OF PM-VBRY 
 
2471. SMT. SMITA UDAY WAGH: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the 
Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY); 
(b)if so, the details thereof, including the number of first -time 
employees and employers who have received incentives under the 
said scheme; 
(c)whether the Government maintains data on beneficiaries and 
employers covered under  PM-VBRY and if so, the details thereof, 
State/UT-wise and district -wise particularly for  Maharashtra, 
including Jalgaon Lok Sabha Constitution; 
(d)whether the Government has introduced special incentives to 
promote employment generation in the manufacturing sector and 
prescribed eligibility criteria for employers under PartB of the 
Scheme, if so, the details thereof; 
(e)whether the Government has put in place a robust Direct Benefit 
Transfer mechanism to  ensure transparent and timely 
disbursement of benefits and if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)whether the Government proposes to expand employment 
generation under PM-VBRY in Maharashtra, particularly in Jalgaon 
Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The Government, on 1 July 2025, approved the 
Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled the Pradhan Mantri 
Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote employment 
generation, enhance employability, and strengthen social security 
across all sector s, with a particular focus on the manufacturing 
sector. 
 
   The scheme comprises of two parts i.e.  Part A and Part 
B, and focuses on providing support to both employees and 
employers by way of incentives.  
Contd..2/- 

 
:: 2 :: 
   Under Part A of the scheme, the first -time employees of 
both existing and new establishments shall be eligible for an 
incentive equivalent to one month’s EPF wage, subject to a maximum 
of ₹15,000. This incentive will be payable in two instalments during 
the first year of employment. The first instalment, up to ₹7,500, shall 
be disbursed after completion of six months of continuou s 
employment. Eligibility for the second instalment shall arise after 
completion of twelve months of employment and successful 
completion of the prescribed Financial Literacy Programme. This 
second instalment shall be credited to an appropriate savings 
instrument / saving account for a specified period.  
   Part B incentivizes employers by providing up to ₹3,000 
per month for each additional employment sustained for at least 6 
months for two years, with extended benefits for another two years 
for the manufacturing sector.  
  All establishments including New as well as the 
Exempted establishments covered under EPF & MP Act, 1952, are 
eligible under the scheme, provided they file the ECR along with 
contributions regularly and fulfill other conditions of the sc heme. 
  Comprehensive Scheme Guidelines, outlining the 
eligibility criteria for incentives to both employees and employers 
have been issued. The scheme and its provisions have been widely 
disseminated through extensive outreach efforts across the country. 
  A dedicated portal (pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in) has been 
developed to facilitate all scheme -related processes and for real -
time monitoring of beneficiaries and sector-wise progress. 
  For effective implementation of the scheme, a robust 
monitoring framework has been instituted. A steering Committee 
with representation from various labour intensive and related 
Ministries/Department and an internal Executive Committee have 
been constituted to ensure effective monitoring of the scheme.  
  The Scheme also provides for a mid -term evaluation for 
necessary course correction and an end -term evaluation to assess 
the Scheme outcome by a third party.  
  The incentives to the employees are paid throu gh 
(Aadhaar Bridge Payment System) Direct Benefit Transfer to their 
Aadhaar seeded bank accounts and incentive to the 
establishments are provided as Direct Benefit Transfer to PAN 
linked bank accounts of the establishments.  
Contd..3/- 
 

 
:: 3 :: 
 
  The State-wise details of beneficiaries under Part A and 
B since the start of implementation till June, 2026 under the scheme 
in the country including the State of Maharashtra, are provided at 
Annexure-I. 
  The District-wise details of beneficiaries under Part A and 
Part B of the scheme, since the start of implementation till June, 
2026, for the State of Maharashtra including the Jalgaon district, are 
provided at Annexure-II.

entries.t: Implementation of Employment Generation Schemes in West Bengal
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2473 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03RD AUGUST, 2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF EMPLOYMENT GENERATION SCHEMES IN WEST 
BENGAL 
2473. MS SAYANI GHOSH: 
 
   Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of employment generation schemes, including the 
Pradhan Mantri -Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM -VBRY) being 
implemented in West Bengal, along with the funds allocated, 
released and utilised since its inception; 
(b) the details of beneficiaries, employment generated and incentives 
released under the said schemes, district-wise; 
(c) whether the West Bengal Government is implementing all the 
schemes related to employment and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the said 
schemes on formal employment, youth employment and women's 
employment in West Bengal and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of measures taken by the Government to improve 
implementation, employer participation and employment 
outcomes under the said schemes in West-Bengal? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): Employment generation coupled with improving employability 
is a priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is 
implementing various employment generation schemes/ programmes in 

the country including the State of West Bengal. The details of various 
employment generation schemes/ programmes being implemented by 
the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes 
 
Government is implementing ‘Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar 
Yojana (PMVBRY)’ to promote employment generation, enhance 
employability, and strengthen social security across all sectors 
including MSMEs and rural enterprises, with a particular focus on th e 
manufacturing sector. The scheme comprises two of parts, i.e. Part A 
and Part B, and focuses on providing support to both employees and 
employers by way of incentives.  Part A of the scheme, incentivise the 
first-time employees of both existing and new establishments by 
providing one month’s EPF wage, subject to a maximum of ₹15,000. Part 
B incentivises employers by providing upto ₹3000 per month for each 
additional employment sustained for atleast six months.  
 
In the State of West Bengal, an amount of ₹25.48 Crore has been 
disbursed to 64,716 first -time employees under Part A of the Scheme. 
Further, under Part B of the Scheme, an amount of ₹68.81 Crore has 
been disbursed to 3,493 eligible establishments for crea tion of 89,297 
additional jobs. 
Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India are 
derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by the 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. 
The PLFS methodology was revamped with effect from Janu ary 2025. 
The PLFS Annual Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to 
present labour market estimates, covering the period from January to 
December 2025. 
As per the latest Annual PLFS reports, the estimated Worker Population 
Ratio (WPR) indicating employment on usual status for persons of age 
15 years and above in the State of West Bengal has increased from 

55.0% in 2022 to 57.4% in 2025. Further, the estimated WPR for youth 
and women were 41.3% and 36.3% in 2025, respectively.  
Further, more than 8.23 crore net subscribers have joined Employees’ 
Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) between September 2017 and July 
2025 indicating increase in employment and formalization of the job 
market. Also, more than 1.29 crore net subscribers h ave joined EPFO 
during the year 2024-25. 
Additionally, Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) 
to deliver skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive 
network of skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. 
under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantr i Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) 
through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims 
at enabling youth of India to get fu ture ready, equipped with industry 
relevant skills. 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has initiated 
‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of IT 
Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies including 
Artificial Intelligence. 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, is 
running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on onlin e & offline job fairs, job 
search & matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, 
information on skill development courses, skill/training programmes 
etc. through a digital platform

(a): The Year-wise details of Budget Estimates and Revised Estimates of PM

In addition, portal has been enhanced by introducing features such as geo-tagging

to candidates. Further, targeted Information, Education and Communication (IEC)

engagement and coordination with States/UTs and industry associations to expand 
the scheme's outreach and participation.

(a) the details of projects approved under the Government schemes for 
the development of prominent religious, historical and cultural sites 
in Madhya Pradesh, specifically in Bhind and Datia, including Shri 
Pitambara Peeth (Datia), Sonagiri Jain Tirtha, Ratangarh Mata Mandir,

wise along with funds approved, allocated and status of projects 
completed and ongoing since the year 2014 to till date; and 
(b) the details of expenditure incurred on the said projects since 2014,

each of the said sites? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM            (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (b): The development and promotion of tourist destinations and 
tourism products is primarily undertaken by the respective State 
Government/ Union Territory (UT) Administration. However, the Ministry of 
Tourism, under its various schemes such as Swadesh Darshan (SD), 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development 
(CBDD) and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation

and experiences across the country including religious, historical and

of Madhya Pradesh is placed at Annexure.  

 
The Ministry of Tourism through its Central Sector Schemes has 
sanctioned various interventions  such as tourist information centre, queue 
management complex, waiting halls, cloak room, widening of approach 
roads, CCTVs for pilgrim safety, foot-over bridges, parking, basic amenities 
such as toilets, dustbins, drinking water facilities and other site 
development works across the country for improving and upgrading overall 
tourist experience. The projects executed under the aforementioned

entries.t: Tax Reforms for Expanding Tax Base
entries.head:
Government of India 
Ministry of Finance 
Department of Revenue 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2479 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 3, 2026/SHRAVANA 12, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
TAX REFORMS FOR EXPANDING TAX BASE 
2479. SHRI BAIJAYANT PANDA: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be please to state: 
 
(a) the major tax reforms introduced during the FY 2025-26 aimed at promoting voluntary compliance, 
expanding the tax base and reducing litigation; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the impact of these reforms on revenue 
buoyancy, taxpayer compliance costs and the investment climate; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to support taxpayers and businesses in understanding and adapting 
to these reforms through outreach, digital services and capacity-building initiatives? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
 
(a): Details of major tax reforms during FY 2025-26 aimed at promoting voluntary compliance, 
expanding the tax base and reducing litigation are placed at Annexure- 1. 
 
(b) & (c):  The tax reforms implemented during FY 2025–26 have resulted in a significant improvement 
in the revenue buoyancy of Corporate Income Tax. The revenue buoyancy of Non-corporate Income Tax 
was muted during FY 2025-26 on account of taxpayer relief measures, including the enhancement of the 
exemption limit for individuals and HUFs and the rationalisation of the tax slab structure. 
The GST rate rationalisation, effective from 22nd September, 2025, is aimed at simplifying the tax 
structure and is part of the Government's continued emphasis on ease of doing business to boost 
consumption in the economy. The reduction in tax burden on essential goods, services, and emerging 
sectors is expected to lower the cost of living, improve affordability, and stimulate consumption demand, 
thereby having a positive impact on GST revenue. Available data indicates that after the implementation 
of GST rate rationalisation, the GST collection has shown continuous increase. Gross GST collections 
(CGST + SGST + IGST) have registered a growth of 7.93% during the period following the rate 
rationalisation, i.e., from November, 2025 to July, 2026, reflecting tax buoyancy. 
However, given the relatively short period elapsed since the rollout of these next-gen GST reforms, it 
would be premature to draw definitive conclusions on revenue buoyancy, as GST collections are seasonal 
in nature. Further, this period was also intermittently affected by geopolitical developments in West Asia, 
which impacted trade and supply chains.  
(d): The steps taken by the Government to support taxpayers and businesses in understanding and 
adapting to these reforms are placed at Annexure- 2. 
***** 

 
 
 
Annexure- 1 
Direct Taxes 
 The Income-tax Act, 2025 and Income-tax Rules, 2026 were enacted to make the law concise and 
easy to understand, with the aim of reducing litigation and boosting voluntary compliance. 
 The safe harbor regime for IT/ITeS was expanded by merging IT services, software development, 
KPO, and R&D services into a single "ITS" category, and it is now available to entities with 
revenue up to ₹2,000 crore at a 15.5% operating margin. 
 The deadline for filing a revised return was extended from 31st December to 31st March 
following the tax year. 
 A time-bound scheme was announced under the Finance Act, 2026 to let small taxpayers declare 
foreign assets and foreign-sourced income and avoid stricter penal provisions. 
 Supply of manpower was reclassified as "payment to contractors" rather than "fee for 
professional services" under Section 402(47) to reduce related litigation. 
 Deductions for PF, superannuation, or ESI contributions are now allowed if credited by the 
return-filing due date under Section 263(1), resolving earlier disputes over what counted as the 
"due date." 
 Assessment and penalty proceedings were integrated into a single common order to enable faster 
dispute resolution. 
 In search assessments, the block period for “other person" was limited to one year when the 
undisclosed income relates to only one tax year. 
 Taxpayers are now permitted to file an updated return even after reassessment proceedings have 
begun, or when reducing a previously claimed loss. 
 Under the Black Money Act, prosecution can no longer be launched for non-disclosure of non-
immovable foreign assets valued below ₹20 lakh. 
Indirect Taxes — GST Rate Rationalization 
 The 56th GST Council meeting approved a simplified two-rate "Simple Tax" structure, with a 
Standard Rate of 18%, a Merit Rate of 5%, and a special demerit rate of 40% for select goods and 
services. 
 The 12% slab was largely phased out, and the former 28% slab was restructured into the new 
40% demerit rate. 
 
 

 
 GST was fully exempted on individual life
